Hold a referendum on re-joining the European Union, I want the government to hold a referendum on whether the UK should Rejoin the European Union., I agree with the government that our country needs growth to get the funding needed to help fix our public services and meet our housing needs.
 
Rejoining the EU, some research says, would grow the economy by far more than  other methods and more quickly.
 
There is a generation who couldn't vote in 2016 and we think now want their say.
 
So let's test this issue, with a referendum.

Reverse changes to Winter Fuel Payment , We want the Government to restore the Winter Fuel Payment to how it was paid last winter immediately. We are concerned that pensioners could die if MPs do not act, and that the NHS could be under more pressure., It has been reported that Labour party analysis published in 2017 said plans to cut the fuel allowance for ten million pensioners could increase excess deaths by almost 4,000 that winter.

Give State Pension to all at 60 and increase it to equal 48hrs at Living Wage, We want the Government to make the State Pension available from the age of 60 and increase this to equal 48 hours a week at the National Living Wage., Hence from April 2024, a universal State Pension should be £549.12 per week or about £28,554.24 per year as a right to all including expatriates, age 60 and above.

We think that Government policy seems intent on the State Pension being a benefit, while increasing the age of entitlement. We want reforms so the State Pension is available from age 60, and linked to the National Living Wage.

Stop Means Testing Pensioners and increase the State Pension, We demand the government stop means testing pensioners, that we think is a degrading and humiliating practice. We also think the state pension should be increased.
We believe that for too long, our elderly have been portrayed by media as merely burdens on the NHS and the modern welfare state., We think that the elderly should be entitled to a decent pension and a comfortable lifestyle as many will have already paid into the system for longer than the rest of the population by now. We believe any Government should have a responsibility toward our nation's elderly people.
 
In the Victorian era, retirement was often only an option for those who had accrued wealth. Are we regressing back to those Dickensian times?
 
We believe means testing is an abhorrent practice that is demeaning and intrusive.

Abolish the basic State Pension, increase the new State Pension and pay to all., We think the government should abolish the 'basic State Pension', put all our elderly onto the new State Pension, and increase the new State Pension to a good percentage of average earnings. , We believe those on the basic Pension should be paid the difference accrued between the basic and new State Pension since the new State Pension's introduction.
Britain's basic State Pension is currently £169.50 per week.
Britain's New State Pension is currently £221.20 a week.
Britain's average weekly earnings (AWE) were estimated at £693 in August 2024.
Stop all foreign aid, I would like the Government to stop all foreign aid. I believe the recent amount of £15 billion is unaffordable.,

Provide day 1 financial support to parents caring for a seriously ill child, We are calling on the government to implement Hugh's law. We want the government to provide financial support to parents who have to press pause on their life to look after their sick child, from the day their child is diagnosed. , Parents often struggle for financial support should they find themselves with a seriously ill child. There is a gap before parents of seriously ill children can apply for financial help. Currently, approximately 4,000 children in the UK spend more than 60 days in hospital every year.
 
If the government were to provide support to those 4,000 parents each year for a 3 month period to support them with the costs before they are eligible for DLA, we don't think it would cost the government much compared to what is spent on other things. We are asking for a day 1 non-means tested grant available for the parents of seriously ill children.

Review the NHS emergency treatment system, We think there should be a review of the emergency treatment system. There have been reports of people being sent home, without proper treatment, and then losing their lives., We think the system is broken. We can’t lose dear people. We need to take action.

Seek to rejoin the European Union Single Market and start discussions now, I would like the UK Government to start discussions with the European Union to seek to rejoin the EU Single Market and to make rejoining the EU Single Market a priority for the UK Government, and to set itself the aim of rejoining the Single Market within 12 months., In 2023, the EU accounted for 41% of the UK Exports, and 51% of imports. The OBR estimates that both exports and imports will be around 15% lower in the long run than if the UK had remained in the EU. We believe that any reduction in income for the UK involved could force the Government to raise taxes and reduce spending on public services. We believe the 52:48 Referendum result meant people may have wanted a softer Brexit, which we think rejoining the Single Market could deliver.

Change rules so parents with 50/50 shared care don’t pay child maintenance, I think we should stop forcing parents with 50/50 shared care to pay maintenance to the other parent. This rule needs changing.,

Provide extra emergency funding into adult social care, We believe there is an alarming shortfall in adult social care funding, which could lead to care packages being reduced and people denied the extra care that they require. We think that immediate additional funding is required to plug this gap., There is already a significant unmet need for social care. Nuffield Trust estimated that fewer than half of older people with care needs were receiving support. The number of people over 80 is predicted to increase by more than 40% over the next 15 years. We are also seeing a rise in adult disability and mental health issues. 
 
We believe that if the adult care sector isn't given adequate funding now it will reach a crisis point, with no chance of it being able to meet the higher need in the future.

Make disclosing someone else’s HIV status illegal, We think the Government should protect people who disclose their HIV status to Sexual Partners or peers. When a HIV+ person discloses they’re unprotected from gossip. We think it should be illegal to disclose someone else’s HIV status., We think protecting people's status could help increase awareness and reduce stigma therefore helping the fight against HIV.

Increase statutory paternity leave from two weeks to four weeks., I want the statutory two weeks of paternity leave to be extended by two weeks, to four weeks., We think this increase will aid many people, including self- employed workers, people employed in male dominated workplaces (we think these workplaces are incredibly behind the times and not particularly supportive of men taking longer than their two week entitlement) etc.
 
Some firms have recently increased their paid paternity leave policy to 12 weeks, which is a marked increase, but we think all fathers should be able to benefit from more time away from work when their baby is born.

Dual Cab pickup trucks keep commercial status beyond April 2025, Keep the commercial status of dual cab pickup trucks rather than re-classifying them as passenger cars, for those using them for agriculture or construction. They are so important., Some businesses may not be able to afford double cab pickups on a company car tax basis, yet single cabs may not be as useful for working in these industries. The tax status change could lead to more people driving separately, which is worse for the environment. Also, dual cabs are often built to specifications that enable them to tow a heavier weight.

UK Government to open talks with EU on rejoining Custom Union and Single Market, We think the government should seek to rejoin CU/SM as soon as possible to ensure seamless trade., We think our economy is suffering being so distanced from EU, our nearest trading partner.

Exempt Commonwealth soldiers from the Life in the UK test after 6yrs Service., We call on the Government to exempt Commonwealth soldiers in the British army from the Life in the UK test when applying for citizenship after 6 years and more continuous service., We believe that due to the struggles, mental health and stress commonwealth soldiers go through in serving they find it hard sometimes to sit and pass the Life in UK test; and this has caused so many problems in the life of the serving soldiers. 

We have suggested inserting the reference to applying for citizenship because Commonwealth members of HM Forces are exempt from the test when applying for indefinite leave to remain.

Expand the winter fuel allowance to other vulnerable people., Instead of means testing the winter fuel payment for pensioners, we think all over 60s, those with cancer or long term sick patients should be entitled to £100 per month for each of gas and electricity from Oct to Jan paid directly to the energy company, or £200 per month for all electric homes., We believe this could help cut hospital admissions and the associated cost to the NHS.

Negotiate with EU to end the 90 day limit on staying in Schengen area countries, We want the government to negotiate with EU to end the 90 day limit on staying in Schengen area countries without a visa. We think this rule detrimentally affects many people as well as and the relationship between UK and EU.,

Change building regulations to ensure more women's toilets in public buildings, We call on the Government to change building regulations whereby all new and renovated public buildings have twice as many women's toilets as men's toilets. We believe that women requiring more toilets has been overlooked in the male-dominated construction industry., We believe this measure will prevent excessive queueing and inconveniences for women in public spaces, and that the current situation is a subtle example of everyday sexism that the UK could pioneer in resolving.

Increase defence spending by 0.15% of GDP per year, until it reaches 3.5% of GDP, We believe the UK should allocate an additional 0.15% of GDP per year to the defence budget, until it reaches 3.5% of GDP, set a clear plan for doing so, and implement that plan as soon as possible., Both the current and previous administration promised increases in defence spending to 2.5% of GDP.  We think these commitments haven’t been backed up by clear plans. Given the current climate in geopolitics, we think that this 2.5% figure is too low, and that Great Britain must rearm.

Ban online pornography, and the making and selling of pornography, We call for the Government to ban online pornography and the making and selling of pornography. We believe this would help many young men and prevent future generations from becoming addicted to pornography. We believe it has no benefit to society and must be banned., We believe pornography is a massive issue affecting young men. Millions of people across the world watch. We believe it can damage mental health and contribute to loneliness, and lead to increased sexual violence.

Raise the Personal Allowance for pensioners from £12,570 to at least £25,000, We want the government to raise the Personal Allowance for pensioners (the income you do not have to pay tax on) from the current rate of £12,570 to at least £25,000., We think this would support our older citizens, many of whom have already contributed by paying tax during their working life.

Uprate state pensions for all UK pensioners living overseas, Many UK citizens have emigrated to other countries, like Canada, and now are retired and rely on their UK state pensions for financial support. Only pensioners living in the US, EU and some other countries that the UK has a bilateral social security agreement with have their state pensions uprated., We call on the UK government to address this inequity and ensure UK pensioners living in other countries, including Canada receive the same annual increase to their pension as those living in the United States, the EU, and other countries with similar policies.

For example, UK pensioners in India, South Africa, Canada, Pakistan, Nigeria and others do not receive increases.

We urge the UK government to adopt a policy that ensures all UK pensioners, wherever they live, receive fair and equitable treatment.

Shutdown the Leonard Stocks Centre in Torquay, We are asking the Government to shutdown the Leonard Stocks Centre in Torquay, to protect residents and tourists who visit the town centre., The Leonard Stocks Centre in Torquay should be shut down due to its role as a hub for criminal activities like shoplifting, stabbings, and violence towards locals and tourists. This persistent pattern of crime not only endangers public safety but also deters visitors from exploring and enjoying Torquay's town centre, ultimately harming the local economy and community morale. Shutdown of the centre is essential to restore peace, security, and a welcoming atmosphere to the area.

Deport all foreign criminals with effect immediately., All foreign born criminals serving sentences in our prisons, or released back onto our streets, to be deported back to their own countries., We do not want to pay the costs of imprisoning foreign criminals and we do not want to have them continue to commit crime.

Only provide foreign aid for national disasters and emergencies, We spend 0.5% of Gross National Income (GNI) on Foreign Aid a year. The Autumn Budget confirmed the UK would spend £13.3 billion in aid for 2024/25 and £13.7 billion in 2025/26., Why are we giving OUR money away?

We think we should only use Foreign Aid for natural disasters and emergencies.

The rest should be spent at home. We believe there would then be no need to cut the Winter Fuel Allowance.

Increase defence spending to a minimum of 3% of GDP with immediate effect., We think we must bolster defence given the Russia Ukraine war. We believe that we mustn't think that when the war ends things will go back to how they were before. We think we will need to revert to previous levels of spending, for example in the mid 80's we spent 5% of GDP on defence! 
, Poland has just passed 2025 spending of 4.7%!
Make the state pension the same as the minimum wage for a full time worker, Make the state pension the same as the minimum wage for a full time worker.,

Declare a Bank Holiday in 2025 for the 80th anniversaries VE Day and VJ Day, I would like the Government to declare a special Bank Holiday in 2025 to commemorate the 80th anniversaries of Victory in Europe (VE) Day and Victory over Japan (VJ) Day, marking the end of World War II in Europe and the Pacific., I believe that the 80th anniversaries provide a unique opportunity to honour the sacrifices and resilience of those who lived, fought, and contributed to the war effort during World War II.
 
Many veterans and civilians who experienced the war are now in their late 90s or older, making this potentially one of the last major milestones where we can celebrate their shared sacrifice during WW2. I believe that we as a country owe them this.

Extend Armed Forces preserved pensions to pre-1975 veterans, We call on government to address what we view as a longstanding injustice for veterans who served their country and left before April 1 1975 who don’t receive any preserved pension benefits from the Armed Forces Pension Scheme (AFPS). We would like these made retrospective to include those veterans., These veterans, despite their dedication and sacrifice, were excluded from the pension benefits introduced in later schemes.

Since the introduction of the AFPS 1975 and AFPS 2015, shorter service periods (e.g. two years) have been deemed sufficient for pension rights. We think it is unjust that pre-1975 veterans remain excluded and receive no pension for their service.

Pay pensioners the equivalent of the living wage of a 35 hour week., The full rate of the new state pension is currently £11,502.40 a year, while the annual income derived from the living wage for a 35-hour week will from April be above £22,000. We think there is a distressing discrepancy between these two figures., We must not allow our senior citizens, who have contributed so much to our society, to struggle through their sunset years. We consider that it is a matter of fairness and respect. We all deserve a decent life when we get old. We believe that all pensioners must receive the equivalent of the living wage at 35 hours a week as a minimum. This could ensure a better quality of life for our country's senior citizens and help ensure that no elder person in our society has to face financial hardship.

Allow state pension recipients to claim full carer’s allowance, When you receive the state pension at 66, you are no longer able to claim the full Carer’s Allowance. I would like to see the government allow people who receive the state pension to claim the full carer’s allowance., There are many carers who will still care for there families after turning 66 and will not be entitled or to continue to receive the full carers allowance.

GPSR: Negotiate with the EU to let UK Businesses to Act as an Authorised Person, We ask the Government to negotiate with the EU to let UK businesses act as the Authorised Person (AP) for products sold to NI and the EU under General Product Safety Regulations (GPSR). We think current rules unfairly stop business owners from being the AP, adding costs and trade barriers., The new EU GPSR rules requiring an EU-based AP present a significant challenge for UK small businesses, particularly micro-enterprises and artisans. These requirements may impose prohibitive costs and administrative burdens, which could threaten access to NI and EU markets. By negotiating with the EU to allow UK businesses to act as the AP for their own products, we think the Government could support small businesses, reduce unnecessary trade barriers, and protect key economic contributions to the UK and the EU.

Legislate for a council tax discount for all pensioners, I feel that current council tax rates do not take pension incomes into account. This means some pensioners are having to pay what I think is a very significant percentage of their pension towards council tax., When many pensioners have worked for 50 odd years, paid into a pension, bought their own house, then retire on a lower income, I do not think they should have to pay such a significant amount of council tax.

Abolish fuel payments for mps, Scrap mps fuel payments as they have scrapped the much needed pensioners winter fuel allowance., Pensioners rely on their winter fuel payments. MPs are paid handsomely. This reeks of double standards

Require charities to introduce caps on their CEO's pay, I do not think that those in charge of charities should be earning hundreds of thousands of pounds, when people often donate to charities to help those who need it., I think that charities should give as much as they can to the people/causes they have been set up to help.

Reinstate the Winter Fuel Allowance for those who are paid the old state pension, We believe the Chancellor of the Exchequer should reinstate the Winter Fuel Allowance for pensioners on the old state pension who are not eligible for state benefits., As of 24 April 2024 the full new state pension is £221.20 per week.
The full old basic state pension is £169.50 per week
Each year the old and the new state pensions are increased by the same percentage based on the triple lock so the differential widens annually.
Those in receipt of the old state pension who do not qualify for state benefits are increasingly disadvantaged year on year. We believe the Government should restore the Winter Fuel Allowance to those pensioners involved to remedy the unfairness.

Pension credit: Allow claim if your partner is under state pension age, We want the government to change the rule for claiming Pension Credit when you have a partner who is under state pension age., At the moment, when someone makes a claim for pension credit and their partner, who they live with, is below pensionable age, then the claim is not accepted, unless the claimant is receiving Housing Benefit for people over State Pension age. This can bar pensioners with younger partners from claiming Pension Credit. We think this is unfair.
Make the state pension tax exempt, We want the government to make the state pension tax exempt and not impact the tax threshold., We think it is wrong to tax the state pension.

Defend Brexit Freedoms from Starmer's EU Plans!, To stop Starmer's EU Plans from overturning Brexit and taking us back to square one, particularly with EU fishing rights and our economy!, Because we voted to leave the EU and that vote should be continually honoured!

Do not seek closer ties with the EU, I do not want the government to seek closer ties with the EU. I think they should  consider the democratic vote of 2016. I feel that seeking closer ties with the EU amounts to reversing Brexit through the back door.,

The UK should not rejoin the EU., I believe the Government are again reneging on their pre-election promise NOT to take us back into the EU. Vote for us to remain completely OUTSIDE OF THE EU as voted for in the Referendum., We voted in the Referendum to leave the EU and I do not want the UK to rejoin in any way. Examples; immigration of all types is out of control so we do not want freedom of movement and we also wish to leave the ECHR. The EU has proved to be a bloated vastly expensive mistake and we do not want any part of it.

British citizenship by birth in the United Kingdom for all, Anyone born in the United Kingdom should be eligible for British citizenship, even if neither of their parents are British, or have settled status in the UK.,

The government should build and provide a real time tax spending dashboard, The UK government collected around £830 billion pounds in taxation in 2023/24.
 
Money collected from taxes is spent across numerous government departments to provide services of many kinds for UK citizens. The money collected should be spent as efficiently as possible., We need to ensure that the finite UK taxation budget is spent as efficiently as possible to ensure there is no waste, that the money spent is spent in areas that provide most value for all citizens. I think there are numerous recent examples of wasted spending. It is our money, the people of the UK. How it's spent should be transparent and available for review in real time.

Ban demonstrations/protests on remembrance day 11/11., I would like the Government to ensure no demonstrations occur during the 11/11 and not disrupt anyone from paying tribute to the Armed Forces for those who have given the ultimate sacrifice., I would like the government to back this to ensure we are able to pay our respects to the fallen.

Review the tax system, We think the tax system should be reviewed to reduce the percentage of tax on goods such as food, petrol/diesel, energy etc., We think the review should also consider reducing the income tax rates and changing the rules to mean you do not have to pay tax once you are retired.

We think the government seems to have far too much of the British tax payers money. We think that if the government can afford to spend billions of pounds in foreign aid to foreign countries, and house, feed and clothe illegal immigrants, we are paying too much tax.

Offer the State Pension to all at 60, increase to equal 48hrs at the Living Wage, We want the Government to make the State Pension available from the age of 60, and increase this to equal 48 hours at the National Living Wage. Hence from April 2024 a universal State Pension should be £549.12 per week or £28,554.24 per year as a right to all, age 60 and above., Government policy seems intent on the State Pension being a benefit, while increasing the age of entitlement. We want reforms so the State Pension is available from age 60, and linked to the National Living Wage. If we can't pay a fair Pension, then how can we afford foreign adventurism, nuclear weapons, armies, royals, pageantry, MP's salaries, etc?

Reduce the State Pension age to 63, We want the Government to reduce the State Pension age to 63, for men and women., We believe the State Pension age is too high, and it keeps increasing. People have worked hard all their life and they need some time to start enjoying it, whilst they still have good health to do so. But not everyone has great health or is able to work and we believe this isn't given enough consideration. If people want to work past the age of 63 then that should be their decision.

Allow permanent residents with Settled Status and British familes a UK passport., Spouses of UK citizens that have permanently setlled in the UK should be allowed to apply for British Citizenship without the rigmoral of having to pass tests, or prove they should be able to be British. Especailly for anyone that has lived in the UK for more than 20 years., Many British Citizens, born and bred in the UK, have married overseas nationals. Their spouses have since made the UK their home. Many have lived, worked and paid their taxes for decades. Many have had several children, and even grandchildren. They have built their homes and and whole lives around a British family, but they are denied citizenship unless they pay for and pass a ridiculous test, and are also denied many other rights for which their taxes already pay for.

Apply to rejoin The Erasmus+ Scheme, The Erasmus+ Scheme was a brilliant scheme for The UK and we benfitted so much from being a part of it, leaving it was a huge consequence of Brexit that shouldn't have happened but we can still rejoin while being outside of The EU., Rejoining The Erasmus+ Scheme would let young people in our country have a educational trip across The EU and vise versa for young EU citizens wanting a education in The UK, it's time The UK rejoined Erasmus+ as a part of a closer relationship with The EU.

Exempt spouses with Settled Status from Life in the UK Test, We want the Government to allow spouses of UK nationals, who are permanent residents of the UK with Settled Status, to be able to apply for UK citizenship without having to pass the Life in the UK test or prove their knowledge of English., Many British Citizens, born and bred in the UK, have married overseas nationals. Their spouses have since made the UK their home. Many have lived, worked and paid their taxes for decades. Many have had several children, and even grandchildren. They have built their homes and whole lives around a British family, but they are denied citizenship unless they pay for and pass what we believe is an unnecessary test.

Extend home fee status to everyone who has lived in the UK for half their life, We want the Government to make home fee status for tuition fees available to anyone who has lived in the UK for half of their life, even if they have already enrolled as an international student., Some students, who have been resident in the UK for a long period of time but don’t have UK citizenship or settled status, are forced to pay international tuition fees even when their families cannot afford them and the student has spent their formative years in the UK. Students also have to be eligible for home fee status at the start of their course, so someone cannot benefit from home fee status at all if they have started their course as an international student.

Require weekly public votes on public spending
 
, I think that the British public should be able to take part in weekly votes to determine how taxes are spent.
 
,

Extend the Warm House Discount criteria to cover all receiving benefits, We would like the Government to extend the Warm Home Discount criteria to cover all receiving benefits, regardless of what benefits or energy efficiency rating they have. We would like all those on benefits to be entitled to this support., Many people have lost their Warm Home Discount due to the Winter 22/23 changes. Many people are no longer eligible to support of £150 towards our bills, that we cannot make up.

support the right of photographers to take pictures and videos, We hope that all the people will not be monitored in Uk. As those people are from People’s Republic of China, we hope to review the status and rights of Chinese in Uk again regarding this issue, China has no right to control us in the UK, nor has the right to tell the British people how to behave

Reconsider the nips for the a20 sidcup bypass crittals corner, We would like you to reconsider the fines and penalties given for speeding on the a20 sidcup bypass. Inadequately signed and a 50mph sign still present between the new 40mph that have gone up since people have complained. Many people in the same situation and at risk of losing jobs etc, Unfortunately London transport went ahead and turned on the cameras prior to any consultation and knew that there was inadequate signage etc.
TfL had also said that they would not be issuing any fines until the signage had been improved.
None of this has happened and fines have been given. Many people are at risk of losing jobs etc in this cost of living crisis that we already have.we ask parliament to re look at this and do the right thing in not issuing the fines and points.

Allow the public to own and carry guns for self-defence, I want the Government to amend firearms legislation to give members of the public the right to own and carry guns for self-defence., I believe the Government, army and policy are unable to keep us safe, and that the people should therefore be given the right to defends themselves by owning and carrying guns.

Provide all pensioners born before April 1951 with the new State Pension, We would like the Government to provide all pensioners born before 6 April 1951 with the new state pension. The full new State Pension is over £200 more a month than the full basic pension. We believe this is unfair, and unjustifiable., We are expected to survive on less than other pensioners. We would like the same pension entitlement as people who receive the new State Pension.

Require pension providers to allow early access for retirement due to ill health, I would like the Government to require all private pension providers to allow people earlier access to their pensions if they can no longer work due to ill health, and the pension should be based on their original hours (not reduced hours they worked because of their health)., The Government should legislate to require providers to allow people to gain early access to their pension if they are unwell. After a specific period of time, if they have not improved, or have worsened, they become entitled to access their pension, based on their original hours. This policy could help people with long covid that are no longer able to work.

Extend the Financial Services Compensation Scheme to all UK pension schemes, We would like the UK Government to extend the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) to cover all UK-based pension schemes, We would like this to happen because the effects of losing a pension, and the mental and emotional impact this may have, can be unmeasurable.

Extend rights to home fee status for Children of Turkish Workers/Businesspersons, We want children of Turkish workers/businesspersons to be entitled to home fee status for higher education if they arrived in the UK after 31 December 2020 due to pandemic-related delays by the Home Office, provided that the visa to enter the UK was applied for before that date., We believe current rules for home fee status are unfair, particularly as they apply retrospectively to the children of people who had already applied for visas to come to the UK. We aim for these children to qualify for home fee status, if not this will mean they face higher fees that could prevent these children, who already are on the path to becoming UK citizens from receiving further education. This could jeopardize their education despite meeting the UK residency and study criteria.

Do not introduce new offences relating to wearing face coverings at protests, The Government has said it will introduce a new offence to empower officers to arrest individuals who disregard orders to remove face coverings, with those who flout the rules facing a month behind bars and a £1,000 fine., We believe this new offence will hugely impact protest rights for people who wear face coverings for health or religious reasons, and could result in more non-violent protestors being criminalised. Recently, there have already been several new laws imposing protest restrictions. By signing, you can make it clear that you believe 'enough is enough', We will not stand by whilst the Government chips away at our freedoms, freedoms which, once lost, may prove very difficult to regain.

Increase funding for men's mental health, We want the Government to take men's mental health more seriously, and increase funding to raise awareness of men's mental health, and increase mental health support., Too many men have been struggling with little or no support for too long. We want this to change.
 
We want dedicated funding for raising awareness of men's mental health and improving support.
 
Because too many men are suffering in silence. Suicide is one of the biggest causes of death for men.
 
This country needs to look after its men!

Increase funding to prevent coastal erosion , We would like the Government to increase funding to prevent coastal erosion. We want local councils to be able to access funds so that they can protect coastlines with sea defences. , The East of the UK has some of the fastest eroding coastline in Europe. How far is the government willing to let those be eaten away? People are losing their homes and businesses to it because of what we believe is inadequate action.

Increase alcohol tax and use revenue for improving mental health services, Increase taxes on alcohol, as this is linked to poor mental and physical health. The additional revenue should be used to fund improved mental health services. , We believe that it is an issue that is well worth addressing because it is something that potentially affects everyone in some way even if it is not themselves suffering from it. After looking into this matter we think that this would be the best thing to do to raise awareness about the impact of alcohol and increase funding for mental health services.

Provide funds from Proceeds of Crime Act to police charities and not-for-profits, We propose a policy that allocates a portion of funds seized under the Proceeds of Crime Act to organisations that support the welfare, recovery, and wellbeing of serving and retired police officers and staff who are injured, living with disability or mental health issues and need ongoing support., We believe there are not enough opportunities for charities and not-for-profit organisations to access financial aid to help officers and staff through recovery of physical or psychological conditions or disabilities. Many police officers pay in to federations and treatment centres out of their own salaries, and the public already fund the police through taxes. We would like to see some proceeds of criminal activity help provide ongoing care through treatment for our community.

Give 500,000 UK overseas State Pensioners with frozen pensions parity, We want the Government to increase the pension of all people receiving the State Pension no matter where they live in the world., Pensioners like myself have worked our entire life, paid into the system taxes, national insurance and any other payments due. We have now reached a point where we need our pensions paid to support us. It shouldn't matter where we live as we have contributed to our pension through the system our whole working life. We believe the non-payment of increases for pensioners living abroad in certain countries is downright immoral. We think the only justification for this is that the government wishes to save money. We are only asking for what we believe we are entitled to, nothing less nothing more.

Apply the MOD housing reform as intended on 11th March 2024, Implement the MOD housing reform as intended on the 11th March. This is a retention bonus and in the best interest of the majority of serving personnel., The housing reform is vital to keeping up with society and housing serving personnel on a needs based system. Also aligning serving personnel in a recognised long term relationship with those married brings the army up to date with social norms and caters for the modern family unit. If this policy change is delayed it will have a negative effect on the biggest problems the Army is currently facing, recruitment, retention and moral.

Require new minimum wages be paid from 1 April irrespective of pay period, We want the Government to amend rules that allow old minimum wages to be paid after 1 April if the relevant pay period started before 1 April, so that the minimum wage has to be paid from 1 April, irrespective of when the pay period began., Companies are able to pay staff for less than the minimum wage if the relevant pay period started before 1 April. This means that workers can lose out on significant pay increases. We believe that this unacceptable.

Allow families of armed forces personnel access to Defence Dental Services, Allow the families of armed forces personnel access to the Defence Dental Services at the duty station where the service person is serving, without exception., As the armed forces move around, their families support them and move with them. It’s hard for dependants to find an NHS dentist. We believe they should be given access to Defence Dental Services at all locations. Then when the service person moves to a station, their dependants can then have access to the new duty dental services without worrying about finding one close.

Do not class the State Pension as a Benefit, I feel that the State Pension is not a benefit but a payment you receive back that you have paid into since you started working.
 
, I think it feels degrading that you have reached Pension age and are being classed as receiving a Benefit. We paid into this system to ensure we received money when we retired.

Seek rights for UK citizens who pay into South Korean pension to be refunded, Nationals of some countries are entitled to refunded pension payments as a lump sum after they leave the country or when they retire. British citizens are at a disadvantage as they do not have this right. Many do not pay into the UK pension as they do not work in the UK.,

Protect the Union Flag of the United Kingdom from change or defacement, We want the Government to protect in law the long held traditional colour and design of the Union Flag of Britain and to make it unlawful to change or deface this in any format., Because it stands for British heritage, custom and values.
 
Many brave men and women have fought and died to protect this country and others under the Union Flag and we believe no one should have the right to change or deface it.

State Pension is below the minimum wage payment. Stop tax on pension incomes, State pension (£11500) paid is below the government minimum working allowance (£20820).  Pensioners have paid towards their State pension in tax and NI payment's. Other pensions paid take people across the lower tax band and tax is paid again. Stop tax on all pension incomes., Pensioners have contributed to the wealth of the country and are now being penalised for paying into pensions that we have all been advised /recommended by various government parties to have.  Once we pay over the lower tax band we pay tax again on our pensions that we have paid into. Stop pensioners paying tax on pension incomes so that we can meet the minimum wage requirement.

Give all state pensioners the new State Pension, I’m a WASPI woman that was affected by State Pension change like plenty of other Women and also missed out on the new State Pension on the 6th April 2016. I believe it is not right that pensioners who are on the new pension can get over £200 a month more., I think it’s not right that people who have worked all their lives and some who have been on benefits all of their lives get more pension. We believe this is unfair.

Fund stray dog centres across England, If a stray dog is not claimed at the pound within 7 days and there is no rescue space available, the dog is at risk of being put to sleep. We think that stray dog centres should be opened across England to help prevent dogs from being destroyed. , Some dogs are put to sleep after 7 days of being picked up by the Dog Warden if they are not rehomed or claimed.

Create fast-track citizenship route for soldiers from commonwealth & families, People from the commonwealth serving in the British army, both men and women alike, and their families supporting them must fill many requirements in order to achieve UK citizenship. We think this should change. , We believe the UK government should implement a law and or programme that allows soldiers from commonwealth countries, serving with the British army, the right to fast track citizenship for them and their families should they choose to apply. We think this would not only boost the ties between our communities but also allow our commonwealth soldiers to be seen as equals and given the respect and credit they deserve, for after all they do the same job.

Install a British ‘iron dome’ missile defence system, Increase spending in defence to install this defence system as a matter of urgency., To protect British citizens and property from what we believe is an ever increasing threat of missile and drone attacks.

Increase defence spending to 3% of GDP, The world is more volatile now than it has been in decades. We believe our national defence spending is below where it should be for a top tier military country. I want the Government to increase the GDP spending on defence to 3%., This is an issue of national importance because our defence is priority to many voters. We want more investment so the UK can be more prepared both for physical attacks and cyber from hostile states. This increase could allow more defences to be implemented and to protect our country's security.

Seek to rejoin the European Union , We would like the Government to seek to rejoin the European Union. We believe negotiations for re-entry should commence. , We would like to rejoin the EU as we think that Brexit has manifestly failed to deliver the benefits it promised.

Do not remove British citizenship from UK-born dual nationals, We do not want the Government to remove British citizenship from UK-born dual nationals. UK-born dual citizens can be deprived of their British citizenship. We believe this creates a sense of mistrust among immigrant communities and alienates them from the British state., There are effectively two classes of British citizenship, and only dual nationals can be deprived of citizenship this way. We think that UK-born dual nationals should always retain their right to British citizenship, and that it is in the public interest that UK citizens with dual nationalities should have their citizenship protected.

Disregard all military pension schemes for tax and other benefit entitlements, Military pensions are subject to income tax, and many state benefits are reduced due to income from military pensions, including the War Disablement Pension and associated supplements. We think all military pensions should be disregarded for calculating tax and other benefit entitlements., Potential recruits need to see that their country values their commitment for their lifetime.

Fund free or heavily discounted solar panels for community leisure centres, Provide funding to enable community leisure centres to apply for free (or heavily discounted solar panels)., We believe our leisure centres are struggling with the energy crisis to heat pools and run air conditioning systems, and as a result many are closing or having to increase prices which can make it unaffordable for people. 
 
Many of these leisure centres could have large carbon footprints, encouraging them to use solar panels could also help the government reach their net zero carbon targets whilst securing the health of its society.
 
Please help us to help ourselves and don’t let’s these gems of the community fall into ruin.

Increase Army pay by 30% and an additional £1000 per full year served, Give full pay review to all Army personnel, increasing basic pay by 30% and an additional bonus of £1000 per full year served., The Army are not allowed to take strike action and are the backbone of UK security

Improve our roads, Improve all roads up to a standard that should be acceptable.
In Birmingham for example, out of 10 roads visited (dual carriageways, single lane roads, urban roads and the M6) 7 out of 10 had some deep potholes, shallow potholes, surface deterioration, edge failure, cracking, rutting and subsidence, Revenue received was £7.2billion in the 2023-24 tax year, £4.5billion spent on road maintenance, the £2.7billion difference was used to help fund education, health care and local councils (as per govt fg)
Vehicles on the road to date is 41.3 million
If the revenue is £7.2billion from road tax, that money should be allocated directly to improving and maintaining the roads and not spent as per the deficit. Thus a shortfall works on the roads not being completed hence the condition of the roads
